title: Chemical Bonding

notes.heading: 1. Ionic Lattice, Fajans' Polarizability Rules & VSEPR Hybridization
notes.proseLatex: Ionic bonding is favoured by low ionization enthalpy, high electron gain affinity, and large lattice energy ($\propto \frac{q^+ q^-}{r^+ + r^-}$). By Fajans' rules, a small highly-charged cation + large polarizable anion increases covalent character ($\text{LiCl} > \text{NaCl} > \text{KCl}$; $\text{AlCl}_3 > \text{MgCl}_2 > \text{NaCl}$). Steric number $\text{SN} = \frac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)$ gives hybridization: $2\to sp$ (linear $180^\circ$), $3\to sp^2$ (trigonal planar $120^\circ$), $4\to sp^3$ ($\text{CH}_4\;109.5^\circ > \text{NH}_3\;107^\circ > \text{H}_2\text{O}\;104.5^\circ$ as $\text{LP--LP} > \text{LP--BP} > \text{BP--BP}$), $5\to sp^3d$, $6\to sp^3d^2$.

keyFormulas.label: Steric Number Hybridization Formula
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Predict hybridization and molecular shape of SF4, XeF2,XeF4, I3-, ClF3.

examples.problemLatex: Find the hybridization, lone pairs on Xe, and molecular shape of $\text{XeF}_4$.
stepsLatex: With $4$ bond pairs and $6 - 4 = 2$ trans lone pairs, molecular shape is square planar (dipole moment $\mu = 0$).

notes.heading: 2. Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT), Bond Order & O₂ Paramagnetism
notes.proseLatex: For homonuclear diatomics ($Z_{\text{total}} \le 14$: $\text{B}_2, \text{C}_2, \text{N}_2$), $\pi_{2p}$ lies below $\sigma_{2p_z}$; for $Z_{\text{total}} > 14$ ($\text{O}_2, \text{F}_2$), $\sigma_{2p_z}$ lies below $\pi_{2p}$. Bond order is $\text{BO} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)$: higher $\text{BO}$ means shorter bond length and higher bond dissociation energy ($\text{BO}=0$ means molecule does not exist, e.g. $\text{He}_2$). Critically, MOT explains that $\text{O}_2$ ($\text{BO}=2$) and $\text{B}_2$ ($\text{BO}=1$) are PARAMAGNETIC due to two unpaired $\pi^*$ / $\pi$ electrons!

keyFormulas.label: MOT Bond Order & O₂ Series Ordering
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Rank bond order, bond length, and paramagnetism of diatomic species.

notes.heading: 3. Dipole Moment & Intermolecular vs Intramolecular Hydrogen Bonding
notes.proseLatex: Vector dipole moment $\vec{\mu} = q\vec{d}$ ($1\text{ D} = 3.336\times 10^{-30}\text{ C\,m}$) cancels to ZERO in symmetric geometries ($\text{CO}_2, \text{BF}_3, \text{CCl}_4, \text{XeF}_4, \text{XeF}_2$). Notice $\mu(\text{NH}_3) > \mu(\text{NF}_3)$ because the lone-pair dipole adds to $\text{N--H}$ bond dipoles in $\text{NH}_3$ but opposes $\text{N--F}$ bond dipoles in $\text{NF}_3$! Intermolecular H-bonding ($\text{H--F, H--O, H--N}$) raises boiling point ($\text{H}_2\text{O} \gg \text{H}_2\text{S}$), whereas intramolecular H-bonding in *o*-nitrophenol makes it MORE steam-volatile than *p*-nitrophenol.

keyFormulas.label: Dipole Moment & Percent Ionic Character
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compare NH3 vs NF3 dipoles, cis vs trans isomers, and H-bonding boiling trends.

wbjeebTraps: Classic MOT trap: $\text{O}_2$ ($16\,e^-$) and $\text{B}_2$ ($10\,e^-$) are PARAMAGNETIC despite having an even total number of electrons!
$\mu(\text{NH}_3 = 1.47\text{ D}) > \mu(\text{NF}_3 = 0.24\text{ D})$ even though fluorine is more electronegative than hydrogen.

conceptPrimer.heading: Ionic Lattices & the Lattice-Energy Lever
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Ionic bonding is favoured by low ionization enthalpy, high electron-gain enthalpy and large lattice energy $U \propto \frac{q^+q^-}{r^+ + r^-}$: higher charges and smaller ions bind tighter. Micro-check: LiF beats LiI in lattice energy because $r^-$ shrinks.

conceptPrimer.heading: Fajans' Rules: When Ionic Turns Covalent
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: A small, highly charged cation polarizes a large, polarizable anion: covalent character rises as $\text{LiCl} > \text{NaCl} > \text{KCl}$ and $\text{AlCl}_3 > \text{MgCl}_2 > \text{NaCl}$. Cation charge up or size down $\Rightarrow$ more covalent. Micro-check: $\text{AgCl}$ is more covalent than $\text{NaCl}$ ($\text{Ag}^+$ smaller, $18e^-$ shell).

conceptPrimer.heading: Steric Number = Hybridization (VSEPR)
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\text{SN} = \frac{1}{2}(V + M - C + A)$ counts $\sigma$-domains: $2\to sp$ (linear $180^\circ$), $3\to sp^2$ (trigonal planar $120^\circ$), $4\to sp^3$, $5\to sp^3d$, $6\to sp^3d^2$. Lone pairs compress angles: $\text{CH}_4\;109.5^\circ > \text{NH}_3\;107^\circ > \text{H}_2\text{O}\;104.5^\circ$. Micro-check: $\text{XeF}_4$: $\text{SN} = \frac{8+4}{2} = 6$, two lone pairs $\Rightarrow$ square planar.

conceptPrimer.heading: MOT: Bond Order from Electron Counting
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\text{BO} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)$. For $Z_{\text{total}} \le 14$ ($\text{B}_2,\text{C}_2,\text{N}_2$) $\pi_{2p}$ sits below $\sigma_{2p_z}$; above $14$ ($\text{O}_2,\text{F}_2$) the order flips. Higher BO $\Rightarrow$ shorter bond, larger dissociation energy; $\text{BO} = 0$ (e.g. $\text{He}_2$) means the molecule does not exist. Micro-check: $\text{N}_2$: $\frac{10-4}{2} = 3$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Paramagnetism: the MOT Payoff
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Unpaired electrons $\Rightarrow$ paramagnetic: $\text{O}_2$ ($\text{BO} = 2$, two unpaired $\pi^*$) and $\text{B}_2$ ($\text{BO} = 1$, two unpaired $\pi$) are PARAMAGNETIC despite even electron counts — the classic JELET trap that Lewis structures cannot explain. Micro-check: $\text{N}_2$, $\text{F}_2$ are diamagnetic (all paired).

conceptPrimer.heading: Dipole Moments & Hydrogen Bonding
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\vec\mu = q\vec d$, $1\,\text{D} = 3.336\times10^{-30}\,\text{C\,m}$; symmetric shapes ($\text{CO}_2, \text{BF}_3, \text{CCl}_4, \text{XeF}_4$) cancel to zero, and $\mu(\text{NH}_3) = 1.47\,\text{D} > \mu(\text{NF}_3) = 0.24\,\text{D}$ because the lone-pair dipole adds to $\text{N-H}$ but opposes $\text{N-F}$. Intermolecular H-bonds raise boiling points ($\text{H}_2\text{O} \gg \text{H}_2\text{S}$); intramolecular H-bonds make $o$-nitrophenol MORE steam-volatile than $p$-nitrophenol. Micro-check: H-bond donors need $\text{H}$ on $\text{F}$, $\text{O}$ or $\text{N}$.

memoryHooks: Lattice energy: charges up, radii down.
Fajans: small hot cation distorts big soft anion.
$\text{BO} = (N_b - N_a)/2$; zero BO means no molecule.
Lone pair adds in $\text{NH}_3$, opposes in $\text{NF}_3$.
Intra-H-bond: steam volatile; inter-H-bond: high boiling.
commonMistakes: Counting lone pairs as bond domains without doubling their electron share.
Forgetting the $-C$ or $+A$ correction in steric number.
Predicting $\text{O}_2$ diamagnetic from a Lewis double bond.
Swapping the MOT ordering at 14 electrons.
Calling $\mu(\text{NF}_3)$ larger because F is more electronegative.
Treating bond order as integer-only ($\text{O}_2^-$ is $1.5$).
Claiming intramolecular H-bonds raise boiling points.
Missing that $\text{CCl}_4$ and $\text{BF}_3$ have zero dipole.
examChecklist: Compute SN with the correct $C$ and $A$ signs.
Convert SN to hybridization and shape (incl. lone pairs).
Count $N_b$, $N_a$ for bond order and magnetism.
Apply Fajans by cation charge and size.
Vector-add bond and lone-pair dipoles for $\mu$.
Convert between Debye and SI for dipole questions.
Distinguish intra- vs intermolecular H-bond effects.
